slides.text: I was born with a cruel and useless curse. Whenever my bare skin touched another person's, I instantly experienced a vivid, paralyzing vision of exactly how our relationship would end. I saw bitter screaming matches, quiet betrayals, and tearful train station departures before I even learned their names. To protect my heart, I became a phantom. I wore thick leather gloves in the summer and never let anyone close enough to shatter me. Then came Elias.

Elias was sunlight personified. He worked at the chaotic animal shelter I volunteered at, always covered in mud, laughing wildly, and trying to pull me into his bright orbit. I dodged his accidental brushes for months, terrified of seeing the inevitable heartbreak that would ruin his perfect smile. But one rainy afternoon, a frightened golden retriever bolted, pulling my leash. I tripped, my glove tore, and Elias caught my bare hand with his to steady me.

The vision hit me like a freight train. But there was no screaming. No betrayal. I saw a sunlit bedroom fifty years from now. My hands, wrinkled and frail, were being held to a warm cheek. I heard a raspy, ancient voice—Elias—whispering, 'Thank you for the best life, my love. I'll see you in a minute.' The vision faded. I was kneeling in the mud, sobbing uncontrollably. Elias looked panicked, until I lunged forward and kissed him.
